analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: Largest Net Selling of Info Tech on Record, What to own when slowing growth meets narrow breadth, Large Drop in S&P Gamma
key_insights: Per GS Prime Brokerage data, Info Tech was by far the most net sold global sector last week, with the largest % de-grossing in 2 months and the largest % net selling on GS record (since 2016). Selling was driven by long sales and to a lesser extent short sales (4.7 to 1).
Fundamental L/S managers were down 2.7% last week (alpha -1.1%), their worst week since July.
The Prime book is now underweight Info Tech vs. the MSCI World Index by -8.4%, in the 23rd percentile vs. the past year.

HFs net bought US Health Care at the fastest pace in 7 months, unwinding risk in the sector for a 5th straight week as short covers outpaced long buys. The Prime book is overweight Health Care vs. the S&P 500 by +10.9% (30th percentile vs. past year, 86th percentile vs. past five years).

Months of pressure from interest rates and concerns about the rising cost of capital have led the equity market to downgrade its growth expectations. GS Prime Services noted a sharp reduction in hedge fund net leverage and a positioning pullback in AI-related stocks.
GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 29% in 2026 and 18% in 2027. Positive but decelerating growth has historically been associated with positive but moderating S&P 500 returns.

In decelerating growth environments, stocks with secular earnings growth have usually outperformed cyclical growth stocks. Among factors, price momentum, positive earnings revisions and low volatility have typically outperformed.

Extremely narrow breadth today cautions against Momentum factor exposure, contrary to the historical playbook. Narrow breadth can resolve through a catch down by recent outperformers or a catch up by recent laggards, and either outcome reverses Momentum. GS's Momentum factor fell 8% this week.

GS's base-case macro outlook argues for a further catch up among some consumer-facing stocks that have recently lagged. Investors worried about a continued catch down should focus on defensive industries with quality attributes.

Dealer S&P gamma moved from nearly +$13bn entering last week to essentially flat/short by Friday. The five-day decline was the largest in four years (Squeezemetrics), leaving the market more vulnerable to near-term volatility until systematic overwriters replenish gamma.
Tail hedging: 1.85m VIX calls traded on Friday, one of the highest call volume sessions since 2018 and a record per the note.
SPX 1-month put-call skew had its largest one-day move higher since Feb 2024.
